questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer:
Experience different nature and meeting new people/friends. 
Bergen is a great city for this, since there is a big percentage of the city that are students.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The nature and the ability to apply for relevant courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Very easy. 
UiB has a very nice website and it is easy to find information. 
But you have to be aware of deadlines and different things, but my impression is that it is easy to talk with the staff if you need help after you have arrived.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
We had an intro-week and a day with presentations from our campus "responsible". 
And there are an office at all campuses if you need help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found a room in big apartment that I shared with 12 other young people.
It was I bit difficult but I found it at
Hybel.no
. You have to be patience and apply for a lot.
My room was in the middle of Bergen and only 5 minutes walk to the school and centrum, so I was very happy about it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
If you live on campus fx at Fantoft I think you will meet a lot of people from around the world. That's not necessarily  the case if you live off campus. I had some great roomies, but I didn't meet a lot of new people through the semester. 
However I was very happy with living in the centrum, and I would recommend it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is a little bit more expensive to find your own room than living at Fantoft. But you can save money on not using the public transport, if you live closer to the university.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You get an email with the procedure. I remember it being very simple. 
You get an account at Studentweb and then apply for courses. 
It is a very good idea to know what courses you can get in advance, and have the prior approval from your university.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
You can email the faculty you are applying and they will help you. 
I remember the employes at UiB being very kind and helpfull when I had some questions about the courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I thought it was possible to get some courses that are obligatory at my home university, but I found out they didn't offer the courses at the autumn semester. So there wasn't a lot of courses to choose from, maybe only 4, and I needed 3.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure that you know what courses you can apply to.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was a little disappointed with one of the courses, ECON116.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
ECON116 Natur og ressursøkonomi was very easy and focusing on old litterature as Adam Smith and Ronald Coase with essay-assignments. 
ECON115 Development Economics was also kind of easy since I already have had courses that uses the basic terms, but also with a lot of new theory that I found very interesting. We had one essay assignment. 
ECON260 was the most challenging course with new mathematic methods and theory. We had one groups assignment and one indiviual assignment.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
ECON260 was very similar to the courses we have at UCPH. It was similar to the microeconomics courses I already have had, but with new theory as Bertrand and Cournot, and a lot more. 
ECON116 was very different from what I know from Copenhagen, with focus on theory from former economist and with essay assignments which I have never tries before at the university. I was disappointed with the academic level.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON115 Development Economics
ECON116 Natur og ressursøkonomi 
ECON260 Industrial organization and competition policy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend ECON115 Development economics and ECON260 Industrial organization and competition policy. 
ECON116 was in norwegian.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Things I needed as new clothes and shoes, but also buying stuff for your room in the beginning and maybe for traveling or smaller trips during the semester.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Alcohol is extremely expensive. 
Food is expensive as well, but I thought it would be worse. But it was probably because of the NOK being very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not use the opportunities, but I think they have a lot of different activities to choose from.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
They have a lot of different sport activities. 
Also many different choirs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend the 7 mountains in 7 weeks, which is a thing Sammen has started. 
Every Wednesday in the beginning of the semester they meet at 17:00 and hike on one of the seven mountains in Bergen.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go for a hike or take the train or bus to different places around Bergen. 
We went for a day-trip to Voss and a weekend trip to Tromsø.
Bergen has a lot of pretty places to visit as Nordnes, Gammelhaugen and all the seven mountains.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. There is not a huge different between Denmark and Norway.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in the intro week "Fadder uken", where you meet other Norwegians who have also just moved to Bergen and are starting their first semester.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Participate in the intro week.
2. Explore the cities and all the nice places and cafes.
3.
Sammen.no
has a lot of different nice offers for the students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Buy some nice hiking shoes and an umbrella or rain-clothes. 
There is a very nice sport outlet in Bergen as well.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The nature. It is very different from what we have in Denmark.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
